feedback.problem:
The mass $M(t),$ in micrograms, of a sample of manganese-53 is given by

$$
M(t)=17{e}^{-0.187t},
$$

where $t$ is the time, in millions of years. Rounded to one decimal place, what is the half-life of manganese-53?
feedback.worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

We're given that $k=0.187.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1/2} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{0.187} \\  & ≈3.7\,\text{million years}.\end{aligned}
$$
